calls.summary: Marcus Bellingham called to order AT&T fiber for a newly built home and asked about the 1 Gig symmetrical plan. Oscar confirmed serviceability, walked him through the no annual contract terms, and locked in pricing with equipment included. Marcus scheduled a new fiber installation for the following week.

Priya Nandakumar lives outside a fiber area and wanted a home internet option that did not require a wired line. Lila explained AT&T Internet Air, the plug-in 5G gateway, and the bundled rate near 47 dollars. Priya agreed to switch and booked a new Internet Air installation.

Devon Ashworth called to check the order status on his iPhone 17 Pro that he bought on installments with an eligible trade-in. Rosey located the order, confirmed the trade-in credit had posted, and gave him a shipping window of 24 to 48 hours. No new service was scheduled on the call.

Alicia Fontenot is a brand new customer who called to set up home internet and a wireless line after moving into the area. Lee collected her name, service address, and preferred plan, then walked her through the fiber options and the AT&T Guarantee. Lee scheduled her fiber installation and confirmed her contact details for the technician visit.

Grant Whitfield wanted to switch to AT&T and asked about the offer to cover up to 800 dollars per line to break his current contract. Mary confirmed his eligibility and paired the switch with a fiber home internet order. Grant scheduled a new fiber installation before ending the call.

Naomi Trujillo asked whether Internet Air was available at her rural address and if she could add a device on a trade-in. Mike confirmed 5G coverage, explained the gateway setup, and reviewed the trade-in credit on her old phone. Naomi booked a new Internet Air installation for the weekend.

Harold Metcalfe disputed a charge on his latest bill that pushed his Unlimited Extra plan higher than expected. Sue reviewed the bill line by line and found a prorated charge from a mid-cycle plan change. She applied a partial credit and explained the next statement, but no new service was scheduled.

Carla Devereux called about a warranty issue on her iPhone 17 that kept restarting after an update. Jennifer ran through basic troubleshooting and then opened a repair claim under the device protection terms. Carla was frustrated by the wait but accepted the mail-in replacement path.

Trevor Anslow asked why his Galaxy Z Fold8 trade-in quote came back lower than the advertised 290 dollar tier. Rose explained the device grading criteria and the plan eligibility rules for the 0 dollar promo. Trevor was unhappy and said he would think it over, so nothing was scheduled.

Bianca Holloway called because her scheduled fiber installation window was missed and no technician showed up. Lee apologized, confirmed the dispatch error, and rebooked the visit with a priority note. Bianca remained irritated about the lost day off work.

Wesley Caldicott wanted to cancel his Galaxy Z Fold8 order after seeing a better promotion elsewhere. Oscar reviewed the cancellation terms and the trade-in reversal, then processed the request. Wesley declined a retention offer and ended the call flatly.

Dolores Pfeiffer complained that her Unlimited Premium plan speeds had slowed and support kept transferring her. Lila acknowledged the poor experience, checked the account for throttling flags, and filed a network ticket. Dolores stayed dissatisfied and asked for a supervisor callback.

Ramon Vasquez called about a billing dispute after two months of overcharges on his prepaid line. Sue found a duplicate autopay charge and started a refund, but the timeline of five to seven days upset him. He said his last bill had eroded his trust and hung up before finishing.

An unidentified caller reached the line after hours and left a partial message about a home internet outage before the call rolled to voicemail. No agent was available to capture the account details. The message was queued for a next-day callback.

Franklin Ostrander called angry about repeated failed appointments and an unresolved account credit. Mike tried to de-escalate and reviewed the history, but the caller talked over him throughout. The call ended with Franklin threatening to cancel all of his services.

prompts.question: Is the customer trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: The caller is a new customer looking to establish home internet service at a new address. They are interested in Fiber but have not yet confirmed their building receives fiber service, which is the primary problem to solve.

prompts.question: What are the customer's expectations?
prompts.answer: The customer expects quick installation and wants to schedule an appointment within the next two weeks. They prefer a specific time window and want confirmation that the service will be available at their ZIP code.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: The agent should have captured the customer's email address for account setup and confirmed a primary phone number for the technician to use on installation day. Additionally, discussing the AT&T Guarantee upfront and mentioning optional bundles or Internet Air as a backup would have strengthened the pitch.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling AT&T. My name is Marcus Bell. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. I just moved to a new place and I need to set up home internet. I saw you offer fiber internet and I'd like to learn more.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. I'd be happy to help you get set up with AT&T Fiber. This is a great time to switch, and I think you'll love the speeds we offer. Can I start by getting your full name please?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: My name is Jennifer Walsh.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Jennifer, thank you. And just to confirm, you're looking to add internet service at a new address, correct?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That's right. I'm in the Columbus area. My ZIP is 43215. I heard fiber is available there.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Let me check that for you. ZIP 43215 in Columbus. Yes, Jennifer, great news. Fiber is absolutely available at that address. We have multiple speed tiers from 300 megabits per second all the way up to multi-gigabit speeds.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That sounds perfect. What's the pricing on the base plan?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Our AT&T Fiber 300 plan is $55 per month with no annual contract and no equipment fees. That includes unlimited data and the AT&T Guarantee, which means if you don't love your service, you get a credit. Very straightforward.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I like that. No contract is a huge plus. When could you get someone out to install it?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: We can schedule installation quite quickly. What works best for you, Jennifer? Would you prefer morning, afternoon, or evening? And do you have any preferred dates this week or next?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I'm free on Wednesday afternoon after 2 PM. That would be ideal.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. I have Wednesday from 2 to 5 PM available for you. I'll schedule our technician to come out then. The technician will bring the fiber gateway, set everything up, and make sure you're online before they leave.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That sounds great. Is there anything else I need to know before they arrive?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Just have your account information ready and make sure you're home during that window. We'll call you 30 minutes before arrival. Your plan starts immediately upon installation, Jennifer, and you can pay the first month's bill at setup. Any questions for me?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, I think I'm all set. Thanks for your help, Marcus.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Jennifer. Thank you for choosing AT&T. We look forward to providing you great internet service. Have a wonderful day.

callDetail.aiSummary: Jennifer Walsh, a new customer in Columbus, Ohio, called to set up AT&T Fiber at her new residence. Marcus Bell confirmed fiber availability at ZIP 43215 and sold her the Fiber 300 plan at $55 per month with no contract. He successfully scheduled a Wednesday afternoon installation between 2 and 5 PM and explained the setup process and AT&T Guarantee. The agent demonstrated strong product knowledge and appointment-setting skills, though he did not capture an email address or primary phone number for the service record.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, nice structure and calm delivery on this new-customer fiber intake. You nailed the address confirmation and installation scheduling. Two coaching points: (1) Always capture the customer's email early so billing and setup instructions go to the right place. (2) Briefly mention what to expect on installation day, like how long the technician will be there or what equipment to have nearby. These small details build confidence and reduce no-shows. Great work overall.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling AT&T, this is Marcus. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus, my name is Diana Whitfield. I just moved into a new place and I'm looking to get internet set up, and maybe a new phone too.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Welcome to the neighborhood, Diana. I can absolutely help you get connected. Are you a current AT&T customer or would this be your first time with us?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: First time. I was with another provider at my old apartment, honestly their service kept dropping so I'm shopping around this time.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I hear you, and reliability is exactly where we shine. Let me check your address for AT&T Fiber. What speeds do you usually need at home?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I work from home and stream a lot, so something fast. But I want to keep it manageable, what does the fast one run per month?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Good news, your address qualifies for AT&T Fiber 1 Gig at about $80 a month, symmetrical speeds, equipment included, and no annual contract.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No contract, that's good. I really don't want to be locked into anything for two years like my last provider did to me.
highlights: don't want to be locked into anything

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You won't be, Diana. It's month to month, and it's backed by the AT&T Guarantee. Now you mentioned a new phone, are you thinking iPhone or Samsung?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I've been eyeing the iPhone 17. The store down the street quoted me a price but it felt steep, what can you do?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: With an eligible trade-in on your current phone, we can get the iPhone 17 close to zero down on installments, and I'd pair it with our Unlimited Extra plan at $75.99 a month.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That's more like it. Can I bundle the phone and the internet together to save a bit?
highlights: bundle the phone and the internet

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Absolutely, bundling the fiber and wireless brings your monthly down further, and I can even add a Samsung Galaxy Watch9 for $1.99 a month if you'd like.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Let me hold off on the watch, I want to run the numbers by my husband first. But the internet and phone sound great.
highlights: run the numbers by my husband

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's completely fair. Let's get your fiber installation on the calendar so you're connected, and you can finalize the phone at that time. Does Thursday at 10 AM work?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thursday at 10 works perfectly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. I've scheduled your AT&T Fiber installation for Thursday at 10 AM. What's the best mobile number and email for your confirmation?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: It's 214-555-0182, and diana.whitfield@email.com.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, you're all set, Diana. You'll get a text confirmation shortly. Thank you for choosing AT&T, and welcome aboard.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thanks Marcus, talk soon.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Take care, Diana. Goodbye.

brandConversationRules: Intro + offer: Introduce yourself as AT&T's AI agent helping put together a personalized quote for wireless, fiber, or a bundle, mention that new customers can switch and get up to $800 per line to break their current contract, and ask if they'd like to get started.

Qualify one question at a time: Ask one question at a time to learn how many lines or devices they need, whether they want a phone, home internet, or a bundle, which plan tier or device model interests them (such as Unlimited Premium or iPhone 17), when they'd like service to begin, and their ZIP code so we can confirm AT&T Fiber or Internet Air availability at their address.

Estimate then book: Confirm we service their ZIP, share a preliminary monthly price range based on the plan and devices they described, recommend a consultation with an AT&T specialist for an exact quote and trade-in value, propose a specific day and time for an in-home installation, and let them know they'll receive a reminder text before the appointment with a number to call.

qaPairs.question: How much are AT&T unlimited plans?
qaPairs.answer: Our unlimited plans range from around $65.99 a month for Unlimited Starter up to about $85.99 a month for Unlimited Premium, and pricing depends on the number of lines. I can set up a quick consultation with a specialist to build the exact quote for you.

qaPairs.question: Is AT&T Fiber available at my address?
qaPairs.answer: I can check that in seconds if you share your ZIP code and street address. Once we confirm availability, I'll help you schedule an in-home installation.

qaPairs.question: What is the difference between AT&T Fiber and Internet Air?
qaPairs.answer: Fiber offers symmetrical speeds from 300M up to Multi-Gig where the network is built out, while Internet Air is a plug-in 5G gateway for homes outside the fiber footprint. Share your ZIP and I'll confirm which one is available and get you booked for installation.

qaPairs.question: Can I really get the Galaxy Z Fold8 for $0?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, the Galaxy Z Fold8 can be as low as $0 a month with an eligible trade-in of $290 or more and a qualifying plan. Let's set up a consultation so a specialist can confirm your trade-in value and finalize the offer.

qaPairs.question: How does the $800 per line switch offer work?
qaPairs.answer: When you switch to AT&T we can help you get up to $800 per line to help cover the cost of leaving your current carrier, subject to eligibility. I'd recommend a quick consultation to confirm the details and get you started.

qaPairs.question: Do you have deals on the iPhone 17?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro are available on installments starting as low as $0 with an eligible trade-in and plan. I can book a consultation so a specialist can lock in your trade-in and the exact monthly amount.

qaPairs.question: What is included in the phone, watch, and tablet bundle?
qaPairs.answer: That bundle can save you over $2,500 and includes a phone plus a Galaxy Watch9 and Galaxy Tab A11+ 5G each at $1.99 a month with trade-in and qualifying plans. Let's schedule a consultation to confirm eligibility and pricing for you.

qaPairs.question: Does AT&T Fiber require a contract?
qaPairs.answer: No, AT&T Fiber has no annual contract and no equipment fee. Share your ZIP and I can confirm availability and set up your in-home installation.

qaPairs.question: What is the AT&T Guarantee?
qaPairs.answer: The AT&T Guarantee is our service reliability and credit assurance program that comes bundled with plans. A specialist can walk you through the details during a quick consultation.

qaPairs.question: How much hotspot data do the plans include?
qaPairs.answer: Unlimited Premium includes 60GB of hotspot, Unlimited Extra includes 30GB, and Starter includes basic access. I can arrange a consultation to match the right plan to how you use data.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer prepaid plans?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our Prepaid Unlimited MAX is about $65 a month with unlimited high-speed data and hotspot, no annual contract, and no credit check. I can connect you with a specialist to get set up.

qaPairs.question: Can I keep my phone number if I switch?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, you can transfer your existing number to AT&T during the switch. Let's schedule a consultation so a specialist can walk you through the process.

qaPairs.question: How long does a fiber installation take?
qaPairs.answer: An in-home fiber installation typically takes a couple of hours during your scheduled window. Share your ZIP and I'll help you pick a day and time.

qaPairs.question: What speeds does AT&T Fiber offer?
qaPairs.answer: Fiber tiers include 300M, 500M, 1 Gig, and Multi-Gig with symmetrical upload and download speeds, roughly $55 to $245 a month. I can confirm which speeds reach your address and book your installation.

qaPairs.question: Is ActiveArmor security included?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, AT&T ActiveArmor security is included with our unlimited plans for added protection. A specialist can explain the features during a quick consultation.

qaPairs.question: Can I bundle my phone and internet?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, bundling a phone plan with home internet unlocks additional savings, and Internet Air can be as low as about $47 a month when bundled. Let's set up a consultation to build your bundle.

qaPairs.question: What is my trade-in worth?
qaPairs.answer: Trade-in values vary by device model and condition, and eligible trades can bring some phones to $0 a month. I'd recommend a consultation so a specialist can confirm your exact value.

qaPairs.question: Do you have deals for business accounts?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we have offers tailored for Business as well as Personal customers. I can schedule a consultation with a specialist who handles business accounts.

qaPairs.question: How do I get 24/7 support after I sign up?
qaPairs.answer: AT&T provides 24/7 support along with online tools to pay bills and manage your account. First, let's get you set up by booking a consultation with a specialist.

qaPairs.question: Can someone come to my home to set everything up?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer in-home installation so a technician can get your service running. Share your ZIP and preferred day and I'll get your installation scheduled.
